QF.id: AIFM CIII Modern Portfolio Theory and Capital Market Theory_2

question.text: Ms. Priya Shah, Risk Officer at Aravalli Long-Short Fund, is listing the classical assumptions of MPT for her internal model validation memo. Which of the following is NOT a Markowitz-MPT assumption?

answer.text: Investors base decisions solely on expected return and risk.
Investors can borrow and lend unlimited amounts at the risk-free rate.
Given two assets with equal return, investors prefer the one with lower risk.

explanation.text: The Logic: The ability to borrow/lend at the risk-free rate is an assumption of Capital Market Theory (CMT), not of the original Markowitz MPT. MPT assumes decisions on expected return and risk, one-period expected-utility maximisation, and preference for lower risk at equal return. The Trap: (A), (B) and (D) are listed MPT assumptions on workbook pages 50-51. (C) is tempting because it appears in the CMT section on pages 57-58, but it is NOT in the MPT list. Note: Pages checked: 50-51 (MPT assumptions) and 57-58 (CMT, where risk-free borrowing/lending is introduced). Keep MPT and CMT assumptions separate when answering.
